# Interconnection Queue Challenges Overview: lessons from the field (summary)

Odalys Silvbrook of VoltStor Solutions presented an overview of the persistent challenges faced in the interconnection queues for grid-scale battery storage projects. She highlighted factors causing significant delays, such as extended feasibility studies, disputes over network upgrade costs, and changing interconnection requirements. These issues create a cascading impact, stalling dispatch software integration and degrading model accuracy due to uncertain operational data. Odalys emphasized the benefits of early collaboration with grid operators during cluster study phases, which helped reduce approval times by nearly 30% in pilot projects. She also noted emerging regulatory pilot programs aimed at resolving cost allocation disputes more efficiently. Overall, coordinated reforms involving developers, grid operators, and regulators are needed to streamline interconnection processes and improve project timelines.

- Over 140 battery projects tracked by VoltStor Solutions face interconnection queue delays across three regional transmission organizations.
- Common bottlenecks include feasibility studies lasting over 18 months, disputes over network upgrade cost allocation, and evolving grid interconnection requirements.
- Early engagement in cluster study phases with transmission planners reduced approval times by about 30% for pilot projects.
- Changing grid codes require repeated dispatch software revisions, causing rework and further delays.
- Emerging regulatory pilot programs are testing mediation panels to expedite resolution of cost allocation disputes and reduce queue backlogs.
